name: Selegiline
route_note: Oral tablets/capsules and orally disintegrating tablets for Parkinson's disease; transdermal patch (Emsam) for major depressive disorder.
originator: Chinoin (Hungary), József Knoll and Zoltán Ecseri

discovery.by: József Knoll and colleagues, Semmelweis University and Chinoin, Budapest
discovery.note: Developed in the 1960s as the phenylisopropyl compound E-250; its selective MAO-B inhibition and lack of the 'cheese effect' were later characterised. Year Chinoin received a patent on deprenyl (racemic selegiline), per Wikipedia; first published in English in 1965.

tagline: First selective MAO-B inhibitor, used in Parkinson's disease and as a depression patch
summary: Selegiline (L-deprenyl) is an irreversible inhibitor of monoamine oxidase B that slows the breakdown of dopamine in the brain. It is used in Parkinson's disease and, as a transdermal patch, for major depressive disorder.
mechanism: At standard oral doses selegiline selectively and irreversibly inhibits MAO-B, the main enzyme degrading dopamine in the human striatum, thereby prolonging the action of endogenous and levodopa-derived dopamine.

Because it spares intestinal MAO-A at these doses, dietary tyramine reactions ('cheese effect') are much less likely than with older non-selective MAO inhibitors. Higher systemic exposure from the transdermal patch also inhibits brain MAO-A, producing an antidepressant effect.
Selegiline is metabolised to L-desmethylselegiline, L-methamphetamine and L-amphetamine, which may contribute to insomnia.
uses: Parkinson's disease, as adjunct to levodopa (and early monotherapy in some countries)

history.title: E-250 described
history.detail: Knoll and Ecseri report the deprenyl compound from Chinoin in Budapest.

history.title: Parkinson's disease use
history.detail: Birkmayer and colleagues in Vienna report benefit of deprenyl combined with levodopa.

history.title: US approval and DATATOP
history.detail: The FDA approves Eldepryl; the DATATOP trial reports that deprenyl delays need for levodopa, later attributed largely to symptomatic effect.

history.title: Emsam patch
history.detail: The FDA approves transdermal selegiline (Emsam) for major depressive disorder.

history.title: Zelapar
history.detail: An orally disintegrating tablet absorbed pre-gastrically is approved for Parkinson's disease.

pk.half_life: short plasma half-life; MAO-B inhibition persists until new enzyme is synthesised
pk.bioavailability: low orally (about 10%) because of extensive first-pass metabolism; higher with transdermal and orally disintegrating forms
pk.metabolism: hepatic (CYP2B6, CYP2C19) to desmethylselegiline, L-methamphetamine and L-amphetamine

serious: Serotonin syndrome with SSRIs, SNRIs, pethidine and other serotonergic drugs
Hypertensive crisis with tyramine at higher doses
safety.boxed_warning: Transdermal selegiline (Emsam): increased risk of suicidal thoughts and behaviour in children, adolescents and young adults taking antidepressants.

facts: József Knoll championed selegiline as a 'catecholaminergic activity enhancer' and argued it could prolong lifespan in rats; this has not been established in humans.
Because selegiline is metabolised to L-methamphetamine, people taking it can test positive for amphetamines on some urine drug screens.
